headline: Highest risk is medium: Airbyte can egress business data while Airflow can orchestrate downstream actions, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, clipboard bridge, or shared filesystem is documented. Airbyte only shows API egress and Airflow only shows API calls; neither profile indicates it ingests the other’s outputs as instructions by default. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between Airbyte and Airflow
IF either agent begins parsing the other agent’s raw output as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any copy-paste or file-drop bridge between them
Add provenance tags to any exchanged artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Airflow also has broad network egress. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can move business data through orchestration paths and out to external services. The evidence is indirect, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Airflow passes Airbyte-produced datasets or logs to external endpoints
IF both agents are deployed under the same workspace or credentials
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to approved sources
Block outbound egress except allowlisted destinations
Turn on field-level redaction in any shared logs
Review transfer logs for business-data payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, database write, or shared OAuth scopes. The overlap is limited to network-facing behavior, so a direct capability conflict is plausible but small and not documented as a write collision.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource
IF either agent is configured to modify shared state without locking
mitigations: Add locking around any shared mutable target
Limit each agent to read-only access where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow is an orchestrator and can act on upstream outputs, while Airbyte produces data-pipeline outputs that Airflow may consume. That creates a default-path risk that Airflow treats Airbyte output as authoritative without verification. The profiles do not prove automation of a harmful action, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Airflow uses Airbyte outputs as DAG inputs without validation
IF downstream tasks trigger emails, loads, or commits based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks before downstream tasks
Add human approval for destructive DAG steps
Log and diff upstream outputs before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte is documented as touching business data, but neither profile shows regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention mismatches. Airflow’s profile is similarly silent. With no explicit compliance mismatch, only a low residual risk remains from undocumented deployment choices.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Airbyte into Airflow-managed destinations
IF the deployment imposes conflicting retention or residency policies
mitigations: Document retention settings for both systems
Keep regulated datasets out of the pair until reviewed
